suggestion.title: Malicious npm Package Installation with Credential File Access
suggestion.rationale: Article describes worm that 'steals npm, GitHub, AWS, and Kubernetes Secrets From Developers' — requires detection of npm/Node.js process accessing ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.kube, .npmrc after package installation. Pipeline missed entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on node.exe or npm.exe child processes reading credential stores (~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.kube, .npmrc, .env) within 60 seconds of package installation. Flag any process spawned from postinstall/preinstall scripts accessing these paths.

suggestion.title: Package.json Post-Install Script Network Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article implies malware delivered via npm postinstall/preinstall scripts ('stealing' credentials suggests data exfiltration). Pipeline should surface execution + C2 callback pattern but reconstructed zero kill-chain phases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on node/npm processes making outbound HTTP/HTTPS or DNS requests to non-whitelisted domains during or immediately after package installation. Flag unexpected C2 domains or high-entropy subdomains from npm process context.

suggestion.title: Credential Enumeration via Environment Variables During npm Install
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware targets 'npm, GitHub, AWS, and Kubernetes Secrets' — implies environment variable enumeration. Pipeline failed to map T1552.003 or generate detection for getenv/process.env enumeration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect node processes spawning 'env', 'printenv', or equivalent commands during npm install, or repeated /proc/self/environ reads. Flag code patterns accessing process.env in postinstall context.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Registry Substitution or Malicious Package Version Pinning
suggestion.rationale: Article describes Shai-Hulud as supply-chain attack via npm — pipeline should reconstruct T1195.001 (Supply Chain Compromise) and detect when package.json/package-lock.json references unexpected registry URLs or pinned malicious versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor .npmrc, package.json, package-lock.json for registry substitution (pointing to non-official npm). Alert on installation of packages with unexpected or typosquatted names, or version pinning to specific malicious hashes known in threat intel feeds.

suggestion.title: Multi-credential Harvest and Batch Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article headline specifies *multiple* credential types (npm + GitHub + AWS + Kubernetes) stolen in single attack — pipeline should have generated composite detection combining credential access (T1552) with exfiltration (T1567) but returned zero use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when single process accesses multiple credential stores sequentially (e.g., reads ~/.ssh, then ~/.aws, then ~/.kube within <5 min window) followed by outbound traffic to non-standard ports or to domains outside developer infrastructure.

suggestion.title: npm Package Installation Spawns Unauthorized Credential File Access
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes the attack occurs during package installation ('worm steals npm, GitHub, AWS, Kubernetes secrets from developers'). Detection must correlate npm/node process execution with reads of .npmrc, .aws/credentials, .kube/config, .git/config files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Node.js or npm processes reading sensitive credential files (.npmrc, .aws/credentials, .kube/config, .git/config) shortly after package installation. Establish baseline of legitimate npm credential access and alert on anomalous reads from unfamiliar package paths.

suggestion.title: Multi-Secret Type Exfiltration from Single Developer Host
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names four credential types stolen: npm, GitHub, AWS, Kubernetes. This pattern is highly specific to supply-chain malware targeting DevOps/platform engineers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Single process or child process reading multiple secret file types followed by outbound network connections to non-standard ports or C2 domains. Correlate file access telemetry (reading .npmrc, AWS SDK config dirs, .kube/config) with subsequent DNS/HTTP egress from same process parent.

suggestion.title: Malicious npm Package Detection via Suspicious Post-Install Script Behavior
suggestion.rationale: Worm propagates via npm packages themselves. Article describes active credential theft during installation, suggesting malicious postinstall hooks or binary downloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: npm install or package manager spawning unexpected child processes (shell, curl, powershell) that access credential files or make outbound connections. Flag postinstall scripts executing network-enabled binaries or credential enumeration commands.

suggestion.title: npm Supply-Chain Compromise Indicator: Registry Tampering or Typosquatting Package Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title indicates the worm distributes via npm packages. Requires identifying malicious package names, versions, or registry metadata anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm package.json lock files for unexpected package versions, newly introduced dependencies not in prior snapshots, or packages with recent creation dates and high download velocity. Cross-reference against threat-intel feeds of known-malicious npm packages.

suggestion.title: Kubernetes kubeconfig Credential Extraction and Lateral Movement Preparation
suggestion.rationale: Article names Kubernetes secrets as exfiltration target. kubeconfig access enables cluster-wide lateral movement and should be isolated as high-fidelity indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: File read access to $HOME/.kube/config or KUBECONFIG environment variable by non-kubectl processes. Correlate with subsequent process execution of kubectl or cloud CLI tools that would use extracted tokens.

suggestion.title: AWS Credential Harvesting from ~/.aws/credentials and Environment Variables
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names AWS secret theft. $HOME/.aws/credentials and AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID environment variable reads are high-confidence indicators of lateral-movement preparation in cloud environments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Process reading $HOME/.aws/credentials, $HOME/.aws/config, or accessing AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID/AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY environment variables outside of AWS CLI/SDK context. Establish whitelist of expected AWS credential consumers and alert on anomalies.

suggestion.title: SQL Injection Attack Against Avada Builder Plugin Parameters
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists 'SQL Injection Flaws' as primary vulnerability. Pipeline generated zero detection for SQLi exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST/GET requests to Avada Builder plugin endpoints (/wp-content/plugins/avada-builder/*, admin-ajax.php with avada parameters) for SQL metacharacters (UNION, SELECT, OR 1=1, xp_, sp_). Alert on SQL error messages in responses or unexpected database results following requests with injection payloads.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Read via Avada Builder Path Traversal
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly calls out 'File Read' flaws. Pipeline should detect directory traversal and sensitive-file access attempts targeting the plugin.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for GET/POST requests to Avada Builder paths containing path traversal patterns (../, ..\\ , %2e%2e variants). Alert on attempts to read wp-config.php, .env, /etc/passwd, or database files. Flag HTTP 200 responses with file content following traversal attempts.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance and Plugin Version Scanning for Avada Builder
suggestion.rationale: 1 million vulnerable sites create large scanning target. Pipeline should detect vulnerability-scanning phase before active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on rapid sequential requests to Avada Builder paths (readme.txt, changelog, version files) from single source IP. Detect 404→200 transition patterns indicating version probing. Flag WPScan or common plugin-scanner User-Agents probing the vulnerable plugin.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Upload and Persistence Following Avada Builder Compromise
suggestion.rationale: File-read + SQL-injection vulnerabilities enable arbitrary code upload for persistence. Pipeline missed post-exploitation persistence detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for .php, .phtml, .php5 file uploads to /wp-content/plugins/avada-builder/, /wp-content/uploads/ following Avada Builder exploitation attempts. Alert on files containing eval(), exec(), system(), passthru(), or assert() keywords written by web-server process (apache, www-data).

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration via Avada Builder SQL Injection
suggestion.rationale: SQL injection enables unauthorized database access and credential/content theft from WordPress installations. No exfiltration detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for SQL queries from web-application context (php-fpm, apache) containing UNION-based extractions or INTO OUTFILE statements dumping wp_users, wp_postmeta, wp_usermeta. Alert on HTTP responses >1MB following SQLi patterns or unexpected outbound connections from web-server processes.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Avada Builder Plugin Detection via Version Fingerprinting
suggestion.rationale: Pre-exploitation visibility required. SOC should detect vulnerable plugin versions before active attacks occur.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Execute WPScan or regex-based scanning for Avada Builder plugin version via readme.txt, CSS/JS file headers, or footer comments. Cross-reference detected versions against vulnerability database. Alert on instances running versions below published patch threshold.

suggestion.title: Suspicious OAuth Token Grant to Unapproved AI Tool
suggestion.rationale: Article states OAuth is the primary attack surface: 'Most AI tools request access to Google Workspace or Microsoft 365 through OAuth, which grants them read or write permissions to corporate data.' and 'A quarterly audit of connected third-party apps, sorted by permission scope, usually surfaces dozens of tools the security team never reviewed.' Pipeline missed detecting the authorization event itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor OAuth consent events for grants to AI/ML-related applications (ChatGPT, Copilot, Gemini plugins, etc.) not on approved list. Alert on first-time grants requesting read/write to OneDrive, SharePoint, or mail. Baseline approved OAuth applications and flag anomalies by user role and department.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Browser Extension Installation — AI Tool
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes: 'Many AI tools run as browser extensions and never touch the operating system, so traditional endpoint management tools miss them entirely.' and notes this is a major discovery gap. Pipeline generated zero detections around unauthorized extension deployment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected browser extension installations associated with AI tools (ChatGPT extension, Claude extension, Copilot plugin, etc.). Correlate extension presence with sensitive data access (files opened, clipboard reads). Alert on extensions installed outside corporate app deployment channel.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration to Unapproved AI Service Domain
suggestion.rationale: Article warns: 'A browser-based AI tool that connects to company data through a quick login approval bypasses those controls entirely, because it never passes through the corporate network at all.' and 'A significant portion connect to corporate data through OAuth tokens or browser sessions, giving them access to shared drives, emails, and internal documents.' No detection use case surfaces this external data flow.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track DNS/HTTPS traffic to known AI service domains (openai.com, api.anthropic.com, gemini.google.com, copilot.microsoft.com, etc.) when correlated with recent user login or OAuth grant. Alert on high data volume outbound to these domains or patterns consistent with bulk data copy (document paste, email forwarding to AI domain, code repository upload).

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Classification Violation via AI Tool Input
suggestion.rationale: Article policy guidance: 'Clear data classification rules specifying which categories of data, including customer records, source code, and financial information, should never be entered into any AI tool.' Pipeline missed detection around users actually violating this principle.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor clipboard pastes, document uploads, and message composition near AI tool domains for patterns matching customer PII regex, credit card numbers, source code markers, or database connection strings. Alert on users pasting >500 characters of classified data into AI service textboxes or prompt injection attempts.

suggestion.title: First-Time AI Tool Access by Employee — Rapid Adoption Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article baseline: '80% of employees currently use unapproved generative AI applications at work, and only 12% of companies have a formal AI governance policy in place.' and 'Across most organizations today, employees are running three to five AI tools on any given day.' No use case detects the adoption pattern itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of user's authorized AI tool usage by role/department. Alert on first access to net-new AI tool domain, especially if user lacks prior interaction with that vendor's services. Escalate if access occurs during off-hours, from VPN-less location, or shortly after department receives AI-related email communication.

suggestion.title: n8n RCE Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'RCE' explicitly; this is the primary attack vector. Pipeline must detect attempts to exploit n8n vulnerabilities for code execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious child processes spawned from n8n node execution contexts or unexpected outbound connections from n8n application server ports. Look for process execution with high entropy arguments or shell escapes from workflow definitions.

suggestion.title: n8n Vulnerability Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Title references 'vulnerabilities' (plural); attackers will fingerprint n8n version to identify exploitable instances. No version-enumeration UC was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to n8n endpoints that enumerate version, plugins, or node types (/api/v1/nodes, /api/v1/workflows, version fingerprinting via response headers). Alert on patterns consistent with automated scanning.

suggestion.title: Post-RCE Persistence in n8n Workflows
suggestion.rationale: RCE provides execution context within n8n; attackers may implant persistent logic via workflow modifications or custom nodes. No persistence detection was suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor n8n workflow file modifications (especially creation of new nodes or insertion of scripts in existing nodes). Alert on scheduled/triggered workflows that execute suspicious commands or make unexpected external connections.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration via n8n Workflows
suggestion.rationale: Title mentions 'automation nodes' and RCE; compromised workflows can be weaponized to export application data, credentials, or user information. No exfiltration UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track outbound HTTP/S connections initiated by n8n workflows to non-whitelisted external domains. Monitor database queries from n8n execution contexts for large data reads or credential queries. Alert on workflows with atypical exfiltration patterns (high data volume, unexpected recipients).

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via n8n Integrations
suggestion.rationale: n8n integrations connect to internal systems (databases, APIs, cloud services); RCE-compromised instance can pivot via stored credentials. No lateral-movement UC was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected API calls or database connections originating from n8n service accounts. Alert on new integrations being created post-compromise or credentials being used from unusual geographic locations or times.

suggestion.title: n8n Credential Theft from Integrations
suggestion.rationale: Automation platforms store credentials for integrated services; RCE grants access to plaintext or lightly-protected credentials. Critical gap in pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor access to n8n credential storage (local filesystem, environment variables, managed credential store). Alert on API calls to n8n credential endpoints from non-standard callers or bulk credential reads.

suggestion.title: WordPress Plugin Authentication Bypass Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Critical Wordpress Plugin Vulnerability Exposes Websites to Authentication Bypass Attacks' — authentication bypass is the core attack vector. Pipeline generated zero detections for bypass exploitation despite explicit mention in title.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST/GET requests to WordPress plugin endpoints with HTTP 200 authentication success responses lacking valid credential submission. Alert on session tokens issued outside standard login flows. Monitor for privilege claims (admin role assumption) immediately following failed standard authentication.

suggestion.title: WordPress Plugin Vulnerability Scanning and Version Disclosure
suggestion.rationale: Title references 'WordPress Plugin Vulnerability' — attackers must first identify vulnerable plugins via scanning and fingerprinting. Zero reconnaissance-phase detections in pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequential requests to /wp-content/plugins/ with enumeration patterns. Alert on HTTP responses disclosing plugin names and versions. Monitor for requests to known plugin vulnerability disclosure endpoints (plugin-specific readme.txt, package.json).

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Admin Privilege Escalation Post-Authentication Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Authentication bypass enables unauthorized privilege elevation to admin. Pipeline missed post-compromise privilege-escalation detection despite HIGH severity and implicit admin access pathway.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate authentication bypass attempts with admin-level actions (user creation, plugin activation, settings modification). Detect admin role assumption by non-admin user accounts. Alert on first-time admin panel access from accounts with no prior admin baseline.

suggestion.title: Persistent Backdoor Installation via Plugin Vulnerability
suggestion.rationale: High-severity plugin vulnerabilities commonly enable code injection and persistence mechanisms. Pipeline generated zero persistence detections despite implicit code-execution risk from authentication bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected file writes to /wp-content/plugins/, /wp-content/themes/. Detect PHP file creation containing eval(), base64_decode(), system(), or shell_exec(). Alert on process spawning from WordPress plugin directories with network connectivity.

suggestion.title: WordPress Database Exfiltration and Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Authentication bypass grants direct database access. Title implies HIGH severity with potential for data theft, but pipeline generated zero collection/exfiltration use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for large bulk data transfers from WordPress database processes post-bypass. Detect SELECT * queries targeting wp_users, wp_posts, wp_options. Alert on encrypted tunnels (VPN/SSH) initiated by compromised web-server processes.

suggestion.title: Rogue Administrator Account Creation via Plugin Vulnerability
suggestion.rationale: Common post-bypass persistence: creating backdoor admin accounts. Article severity and bypass nature imply account-creation attacks, but pipeline missed this follow-on detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect wp_users table INSERT operations from non-standard execution contexts. Alert on user creation with administrator role via unauthenticated requests. Monitor for role-modification (contributor → administrator) outside normal admin workflows.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via RxGK Kernel Vulnerability
suggestion.rationale: Article states exploit 'allows attackers to gain root access' through 'rxgk pagecache write due to missing COW guard in rxgk_decrypt_skb'—explicit attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthorized privilege escalation to root from unprivileged processes on systems with CONFIG_RXGK enabled. Alert on kernel panics, out-of-memory conditions, or segmentation faults indicative of page-cache corruption exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: System Configuration Enumeration - RxGK Kernel Module Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Successful exploitation requires running a Linux kernel with the CONFIG_RXGK configuration option'—attacker prerequisite check.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag queries to /proc/config.gz, lsmod calls targeting rxgk/rxrpc/esp4/esp6 modules, or uname commands on Fedora/Arch/openSUSE systems. Alert on sequential enumeration of kernel module state from single process.

suggestion.title: Mitigation Evasion - Disabled Kernel Module Re-enablement
suggestion.rationale: Article documents mitigation via 'rmmod esp4 esp6 rxrpc' but attackers may bypass by re-loading modules; 'install esp4 /bin/false' rules can be overridden.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on insmod/modprobe commands targeting rxrpc, esp4, or esp6 on systems where mitigation disabled these modules. Monitor /etc/modprobe.d/ for modifications or removal of dirtyfrag.conf rules.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Kernel Detection - DirtyDecrypt Vulnerability Window
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies flaw 'patched on April 25'—systems vulnerable if running kernels released before this date on affected distributions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Fedora, Arch Linux, and openSUSE Tumbleweed systems with kernel build dates or release timestamps prior to April 25, 2026. Cross-reference kernel versions against upstream changelog for explicit DirtyDecrypt/DirtyCBC patches.

suggestion.title: Kernel Exploit Family Correlation - Dirty Frag Class Techniques
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'same vulnerability class as Dirty Frag, Fragnesia, and Copy Fail'—indicates related page-cache corruption exploitation family.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate exploitation signals across Dirty Frag/Fragnesia/Copy Fail/DirtyDecrypt family. Flag systems exhibiting multiple page-cache corruption attempts, kernel oops with similar signatures, or repeated memory write anomalies consistent with this vulnerability class.

suggestion.title: Non-Admin User Access to Admin-Protected REST API Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'Eight of those endpoints...never call the [authorization check]' and 'allows non-admin users to exfiltrate stored Git credentials.' Authorization bypass is the root vulnerability enabling the entire attack chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for non-privileged accounts making successful requests to `/api/customize/git-repositories` or `/api/git-repositories/sync` endpoints that should require admin roles. Flag access patterns where authorization is expected but not enforced, and correlate with credential extraction attempts on the same endpoints.

suggestion.title: Bulk Extraction of Stored Git Credentials via API Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article core impact: 'allows non-admin users to exfiltrate stored Git credentials.' The vulnerability permits direct access to credential storage through API endpoints with no authorization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect multiple or bulk reads from git credential endpoints (e.g., multiple `list` or `get` calls in short timeframe). Alert on exfiltration patterns: single user reading all stored credentials, downloading credential payloads, or exporting git tokens outside the application.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Modification of GitOps Configuration via API Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Article states the vulnerability allows attackers to 'tamper with GitOps confi[gurations].' The `update` and `create` endpoints lack authorization checks, permitting unauthorized config changes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthorized write operations to GitOps configuration endpoints. Flag modifications to git repository URLs, branch targets, authentication tokens, or sync policies initiated by non-admin accounts. Correlate with suspicious git operations that follow the config changes.

suggestion.title: Authorization Boundary Probing on REST API Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article reveals nine endpoints with missing authorization checks. Attackers would probe these boundaries before exploitation: 'list', 'create', 'get', 'update', 'delete', 'test', 'listBranches', 'browseFiles' represent a systematic endpoint set.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect systematic testing of authorization on `/api/customize/git-repositories` and `/api/git-repositories/sync` endpoints. Alert on patterns of 403/401 failures followed by successful access from the same account, or rapid sequential calls to multiple git-management endpoints by non-admin accounts.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Exfiltrated Git Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Once credentials are exfiltrated from stored git repositories via the vulnerable endpoints, attackers pivot to git operations. Article implies post-exfiltration impact: 'exfiltrate stored Git credentials' enables downstream git repository access and potential supply-chain attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate git credential exfiltration events with subsequent git operations from external or suspicious contexts. Detect git clone/pull/push operations using credentials that were stolen via the Arcane API, especially pushes to main/protected branches or credential rotations triggered immediately after exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Asset Inventory: Arcane Backend Installations Vulnerable to CVE-2026-45625
suggestion.rationale: Standard asset exposure detection. Article establishes CVE-2026-45625 affects Arcane Backend git-repository management endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all Arcane Backend instances in the environment, enumerate versions, and flag installations that predate the security patch for CVE-2026-45625. Correlate with network logs showing internal access to those instances' REST API endpoints.

suggestion.title: Formie Hidden Field SSTI Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'crafted values into Hidden fields (with Default value → Custom)... were evaluated as Twig during submission handling' — explicit SSTI attack vector with configuration specificity requiring behavioral detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to Formie form endpoints for Twig template syntax ({{ }}, {% %}, {# #}) in form field values. Flag submissions containing template delimiters, filter chains, or Twig built-in functions (dump, cycle, range, config). Correlate with Hidden field submission patterns and user-agent anomalies to reduce false positives.

suggestion.title: Server-Side Template Injection Payload in Form Data
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability mechanism: 'crafted values... evaluated as Twig' — SSTI is the execution vector; payloads in request bodies are directly observable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SSTI patterns in HTTP POST/request bodies: Twig template delimiters ({{ }}, {%%}), filter chains (|raw, |slice), object accessors (_self.env, config.db), and common payload signatures ({{ 7*7 }}, {{app}}). Correlate with HTTP 500 errors, template exception strings, or undefined variable messages in application logs.

suggestion.title: Craft CMS Formie Plugin Vulnerable Version Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article references patch version 2.2.20 for CVE-2026-45697 — asset exposure requires detection of Formie plugin instances running versions prior to patch.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Craft CMS installations with Formie plugin versions < 2.2.20. Query web server logs for Formie endpoint patterns, extract version strings from plugin headers or error messages, or scan web directories for Formie composer.json and version files. Correlate vulnerable instances with public form exposure.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Submission to Formie Form Endpoints with Template Syntax
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Unauthenticated users could submit crafted values' — pre-authentication is the exploitation requirement; combining anonymous access with suspicious payloads surfaces attack activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal Formie form submissions (user-agents, submission frequency, field value types). Flag unauthenticated POST requests to Formie endpoints with abnormal payloads: template syntax, executable code strings, multi-line values in typically single-line fields, or repeating reconnaissance requests to identify Hidden field configurations.

suggestion.title: Detect mistralai v2.4.6 package presence in project dependencies and runtime
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states dropper 'executes on import on Linux'—malware activates when Python imports mistralai module. Detection of package manifests (requirements.txt, setup.py, pyproject.toml, poetry.lock) containing mistralai==2.4.6 and Python processes with mistralai in sys.path is the primary detection vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for mistralai==2.4.6 string in dependency manifests. Detect Python interpreter processes where PYTHONPATH or sys.path includes path to mistralai package. Correlate Python process execution with subsequent suspicious file or network activity within milliseconds of import.

suggestion.title: Hash-based detection for mistralai dropper payload
suggestion.rationale: Article provides SHA256 6dbaa43bf2f3c0d3cddbca74967e952da563fb974c1ef9d4ecbb2e58e41fe81b as primary file IOC; pipeline generated zero hash-based hunts despite this being direct malware indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: File hash detection on mistralai package installation artifacts (likely __init__.py or .dist-info metadata). Alert on file creation/modification matching SHA256 hash or on Python site-packages/mistralai/ files with this hash.

suggestion.title: Network C2 communication to malware IP (83.142.209.194)
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 83.142.209.194 as high-fidelity IOC; dropper likely beacons to this server post-execution. Article states 'IOCs present' but pipeline generated zero network-based hunts despite C2 communication being the exfiltration phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect any outbound TCP/UDP connection to IP 83.142.209.194 from systems with recent mistralai package imports. Flag Python processes initiating connections to this IP within hours of import-time code execution.

suggestion.title: PyPI supply-chain attack signature: version mismatch between PyPI and source repository
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'no v2.4.6 tag, commit, or release workflow run exists in this repository' and 'upload bypassed this repository's normal release pipeline (which uses PyPI Trusted Publishing).' Detection of PyPI uploads lacking corresponding git tags or CI/CD workflows catches supply-chain compromises.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference PyPI package versions against source repository git tags and release workflows. Alert if package version X exists on PyPI but has no corresponding git tag (v2.4.6) or release automation run in source repo.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Python __init__.py modification in site-packages post-package-installation
suggestion.rationale: Malicious dropper executes during Python import, likely residing in or invoked by package __init__.py. Detection of __init__.py file creation/modification in site-packages following package installation would catch payload persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor .../site-packages/mistralai/__init__.py for file creation or modification events correlating with package installation timestamps. Alert if file contains obfuscated code, network primitives (socket, requests, urllib), or code execution functions (exec, eval, __import__).

suggestion.title: Supply-chain artifact integrity: wheel file hash vs. repo source hash
suggestion.rationale: Legitimate releases use PyPI Trusted Publishing with verifiable links to source commits. Article states upload 'bypassed' normal pipeline; detection of wheel files without commit-to-artifact hash chain prevents installation of unvetted packages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: During pip install, verify mistralai wheel file hash against source repository release metadata and git tag commit hashes. Flag installations where .whl file hash does not correspond to any tagged release in upstream repo.

suggestion.title: NGINX HTTP request exploitation for RCE
suggestion.rationale: Article title promises 'active exploitation of critical NGINX RCE' but truncated body contains no vulnerability details, affected versions, or attack vectors. A real NGINX RCE article would describe specific HTTP payloads, methods, or malformed headers triggering code execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor NGINX access logs for requests with unusual HTTP verb sequences, oversized Host/Content-Length headers, null bytes, or regex patterns consistent with known NGINX RCE exploits; correlate with immediate execution errors or abnormal CPU spikes in nginx worker processes.

suggestion.title: Child process spawning from NGINX worker post-RCE
suggestion.rationale: Successful NGINX RCE typically results in command execution within nginx worker context. Article lacks exploitation chain details but execution is inevitable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bash, sh, python, or cmd.exe spawning as child of nginx/nginx worker processes with non-standard arguments, especially if executed from /tmp, sourcing unusual scripts, or running immediately after suspicious HTTP requests.

suggestion.title: Outbound network connections from NGINX worker processes
suggestion.rationale: Post-RCE, attackers establish reverse shells or C2 callbacks. Article truncation masks infrastructure indicators and actor identifiers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unexpected outbound TCP/UDP connections initiated by nginx or child processes to non-standard ports or newly-registered domains; baseline legitimate NGINX egress and alert on deviations within 5-minute windows of RCE-indicative HTTP patterns.

suggestion.title: NGINX configuration file modification post-exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Critical RCE often leads to persistence via nginx.conf tampering, module injection, or binary replacement. Article provides no details on persistence mechanisms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on modifications to /etc/nginx/*, /usr/sbin/nginx, or dynamic module directories; trigger especially if modification timestamps precede unexpected process execution or if file hashes diverge from package baselines.

suggestion.title: Privilege escalation from nginx user context
suggestion.rationale: If RCE executes in restricted nginx user context (not root), attackers escalate. Article text absent; should still model this attack step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sudo invocations, setuid binary usage, or kernel module loads initiated from nginx worker processes or their children; flag especially if accompanied by exploitation signatures or unusual environment variables.

suggestion.title: Mobile Malware Distribution via App Store
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'discovered several apps on Google Play and the App Store that contained a new version of the SparkCat crypto stealer' and '162,275 packages related to mobile banking Trojans' — explicit description of trojanized app delivery vector
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Google Play / App Store install events for APKs with suspicious permissions (credential access, SMS interception, device admin). Correlate installation with network traffic to known botnet C2. Flag APKs signed by publishers with abnormal name entropy or zero update history.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated Rust Library Deobfuscation via Custom VM

Flag APKs with embedded Rust .so files + unusual entropy encoding sections.

suggestion.title: Kimwolf Botnet C2 and Proxy Network Analysis
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'Synthient researchers identified a link between the notorious Kimwolf botnet and the IPIDEA proxy network. This network was later taken down' — explicit C2 infrastructure intelligence missing from pipeline output
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on network traffic to IPIDEA proxy nodes or known Kimwolf C2 endpoints. Monitor for encrypted C2 beaconing patterns from Android devices. Cross-reference mobile device DNS queries against Kimwolf sinkhole infrastructure post-takedown.

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect mobile banking trojans by: keystroke logging on password fields, overlay detection (fake login screens), SMS/2FA interception, and credential manager access. Baseline: legitimate banking apps should not request device admin, SMS, or call permissions.

suggestion.title: Crypto Stealer APK with Embedded Payload Staging
suggestion.rationale: Article describes SparkCat specifically as 'crypto stealer... meticulously concealed, was embedded into the infected Android apps' — payload staging + wallet targeting warrants collection/exfiltration detection

suggestion.title: Trojan-Banker Code Obfuscation Complexity Indicator
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 'Trojan code, meticulously concealed' embedded via 'obfuscated Rust library' decoded by 'custom-built' VM — defensive complexity deserves static-analysis triggered alert
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag APK packages with unusual entropy in dex/so sections, Rust native libraries mixed with obfuscation markers, or evidence of custom packing/virtualization. Cross-check against VirusTotal for low detection rates despite file size/age suggesting distribution.

suggestion.title: Multi-Vendor Patch Advisory Scanning & Triage
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly lists 'Ivanti, Fortinet, SAP, VMware, n8n' with RCE/SQLi/PrivEsc — absent from output despite 'CRIT' severity marker
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for scanning/enumeration activity targeting Ivanti Connect Secure, Fortinet FortiGate, SAP systems, VMware vCenter, n8n nodes post-patch release. Look for version fingerprinting attempts and CVE-specific scanner payloads (Shodan, Censys queries referencing CVE identifiers from patch advisories).

suggestion.title: RCE Exploitation in Automation/Orchestration Platforms (n8n)
suggestion.rationale: Title identifies n8n RCE but no use cases generated. 'n8n Patch RCE' signals workflow node exploitation and arbitrary code execution contexts
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect RCE attempts against n8n node evaluation contexts: suspicious child process spawning from n8n services, execution of shell/PowerShell via expression injection in node payloads, HTTP requests with template injection or code-evaluation payloads to /api/v1 endpoints.

suggestion.title: SQL Injection in Enterprise Application Suites (SAP, Fortinet Web UIs)
suggestion.rationale: Title includes 'SQL Injection' but no corresponding detection use case. SAP and Fortinet web consoles are common SQLi targets in patch advisories
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for SQLi attack patterns in HTTP request parameters (UNION SELECT, stacked queries, boolean-based blind injection) targeting SAP web components and Fortinet administrative interfaces. Look for anomalous SQL in logs from affected versions.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Patched Kernel/Service Vulnerabilities
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly names 'Privilege Escalation Flaws' but pipeline generated zero escalation-phase detection. Ivanti and VMware vulnerabilities often enable kernel/system privesc
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect privilege escalation post-RCE exploitation: monitor for parent-child process relationships with unexpected privilege elevation (NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM from low-priv service accounts), unusual driver loading, suspicious registry modifications to privilege-escalation gadgets (UAC bypass, token impersonation).

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Compromised Enterprise VPN/Hypervisor Access
suggestion.rationale: Ivanti Connect Secure (VPN gateway) and VMware vCenter (hypervisor management) RCEs enable lateral movement into internal networks — absent from output
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-RCE compromise of Ivanti/VMware, monitor for lateral movement: suspicious outbound connections from VPN/hypervisor hosts to internal subnets, authentication attempts using compromised service accounts, unusual vCenter API calls initiating VM snapshots/clones, SMB/RDP pivots from gateway systems.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from Compromised Web UIs & Node Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Compromise of Fortinet/SAP/n8n web interfaces exposes stored credentials (API keys, database passwords, integration tokens). Article context implies credential-store access but pipeline captured zero
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for credential-store access post-RCE: file operations targeting credential vaults (Fortinet credential database, n8n secrets store, SAP user credentials), memory dumping of running services, unauthorized reads of .env/.conf/.xml credential files.

suggestion.title: MiniPlasma Malware Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'MiniPlasma' as the tool; zero IOCs or execution-phase detections generated for this named malware despite being primary intelligence signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process execution, file artifacts, and registry modifications associated with MiniPlasma exploitation tool. Include process names, file paths, command-line signatures, and mutex patterns characteristic of known MiniPlasma variants.

suggestion.title: Windows SYSTEM Privilege Escalation via Kernel 0-Day
suggestion.rationale: Core attack outcome in title: 'enables SYSTEM Privilege Escalation on Fully Patched Systems' describes kernel-mode privilege escalation but zero privilege_escalation-phase UCs generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect abnormal privilege escalation to SYSTEM on fully patched Windows. Monitor for: non-admin process spawning SYSTEM child without UAC prompt, token impersonation attempts (SeImpersonate abuse), kernel driver load anomalies, and unexpected access token privilege levels.

suggestion.title: 0-Day Kernel Exploitation Pattern on Patched Systems
suggestion.rationale: Title states vulnerability works on 'fully patched systems' — critical detail indicating kernel-mode exploitation that bypasses standard mitigations, but no exploitation-phase detection UCs generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Behavioral detection for kernel privilege escalation exploits: anomalous parent-child process relationships elevating to SYSTEM, unusual kernel-mode execution, invalid/forged access tokens, and execution contexts inconsistent with normal administrative activity.

suggestion.title: Avada Builder File Read Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'File Read' vulnerability in Avada Builder. No detection UC generated despite clear attack vector. Pipeline should detect requests to vulnerable Avada Builder endpoints with path-traversal or file-read payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP POST/GET requests to WordPress sites with Avada Builder plugin installed, targeting known vulnerable endpoints (e.g., ajax handlers, form processing) with path-traversal sequences (/../../../../etc/passwd, file://, or local path inclusion patterns). Baseline against legitimate plugin traffic and alert on high-entropy file paths in query/POST parameters.

suggestion.title: Avada Builder SQL Injection Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly mentions 'SQL Injection Flaws.' No SQLi-detection UC produced. Should detect SQL metacharacters and UNION-based injection patterns in Avada Builder request parameters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to WordPress installations with Avada Builder active. Detect POST/GET parameters containing SQL keywords (UNION, SELECT, WHERE, DROP) or metacharacters (';', '--', '/*', '*/') in recognized Avada Builder form fields. Correlate with 200-OK responses followed by large data exfiltration or error-page responses containing database schema information.

suggestion.title: Avada Builder Vulnerable Plugin Inventory Detection
suggestion.rationale: No vulnerability scanning UC despite affecting 1M sites. Should inventory WordPress installs running Avada Builder versions < fixed version (implied in article but not extracted by pipeline).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for WordPress plugins directory listing Avada Builder installed. Extract version number from plugin metadata files. Cross-reference against known vulnerable versions (≤ fixed version per CVE-2026-4782/4798). Flag any host running vulnerable version as immediate exploitation risk and escalate to patch management.

suggestion.title: Database Exfiltration via Avada Builder SQLi
suggestion.rationale: Article describes SQL injection affecting 1M sites; no post-exploitation data theft UC generated. Should detect abnormal database queries from web server process or large result-set returns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor MySQL/MariaDB query logs from WordPress hosts running Avada Builder. Detect multi-table UNION SELECT statements, information_schema queries, or extracted tables being serialized/JSON-encoded in HTTP responses. Baseline legitimate query patterns and flag anomalous high-volume table dumps or credential exfiltration queries.

suggestion.title: GitHub Action Repository Tag Reassignment to Unexpected Commit
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'All Tags Point to Imposter Commit' — detection must catch tag rewriting to commits outside expected maintainer branches or with unexpected authorship. This is initial_access for downstream consumers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when a tag on a public/trusted GitHub Action repo is force-pushed to a commit not authored by known maintainers, not in the default branch, or with timestamps that violate semantic versioning ordering (v1.2.3 retagged after v1.2.4 released).

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Workflow Exfiltrating Secrets via Unexpected HTTP Egress
suggestion.rationale: Article core attack: 'Exfiltrates CI/CD Credentials'. Detection must trigger when Actions access GITHUB_TOKEN, repository_dispatch secrets, or SSH keys and then POST/GET to non-organization-approved domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Actions workflows that read GITHUB_TOKEN or secrets.* environment variables within 2 steps of curl/wget/PowerShell to external domains, or that write secrets to stdout, workflow artifacts, or issue comments.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Resolving Pinned Action Version to Malicious Commit Hash
suggestion.rationale: Threat: compromised tags cause downstream consumers to execute imposter commits. Detection must identify when a pinned Action (uses: org/action@v1) resolves to a commit hash not previously seen for that version tag.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor the first execution of a tagged Action version in your organization. Alert on commit hash mismatch vs. expected release artifacts or when the resolved SHA author differs from the repo's known maintainers.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Enumeration of Secrets and Environment Variables in Actions Logs
suggestion.rationale: Exfiltration requires credential discovery. Attack likely enumerates available secrets before stealing them. Detection should flag 'env', 'echo $', secret file reads not in baseline Actions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Actions workflows that execute shell commands to list/dump environment variables (env, set, export, compgen -v), read secret file paths, or base64-encode and print GITHUB_TOKEN—especially in public Actions or on first execution.

suggestion.title: Commit Author Impersonation in GitHub Action Tag
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates 'Imposter Commit'—a commit masquerading as legitimate. Detection should flag commits with spoofed author metadata (known maintainer name/email but unverified GPG signature) or commits authored by accounts that lack repo write access.
log_sources: GitHub API commit endpoint (author, committer, signature fields)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when a tagged release in a public Action is authored by an account not listed as a repository collaborator, or when commit author name matches a known maintainer but GPG signature is absent/invalid, or when commit was authored on an unusual date/time for that maintainer.

suggestion.title: n8n Git Node Argument Injection (CVE-2026-44790)
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Critical n8n Vulnerabilities Expose Automation Nodes to Full RCE'. Based on corroborating intel in session context, Git node is exploitable via --upload-pack argument injection. Zero detection coverage was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for n8n service spawning git.exe or git process with malformed --upload-pack arguments, especially from HTTP requests containing shell metacharacters or command substitution syntax routed through n8n's Git node handler.

suggestion.title: n8n XML Node Prototype Pollution RCE (CVE-2026-44791)
suggestion.rationale: Session context confirms CVE-2026-44791 involves XML node prototype pollution bypass enabling RCE. Article describes 'automation nodes' under RCE threat but pipeline extracted zero detection signals.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to n8n XML node endpoints containing malicious property injection payloads (nested object literals, __proto__ traversal, or gadget chain signatures) followed by child process spawning from node.exe with command shell interpreters.

suggestion.title: n8n Unauthenticated Workflow Execution or Credential Extraction
suggestion.rationale: Article calls out RCE exposure but pipeline missed authentication/authorization attack surface. n8n credentials and OAuth tokens are typical post-compromise targets; should detect auth bypass or stolen credential usage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to n8n credential/OAuth endpoints lacking valid session cookies, or for exfiltration of .json credential files and .env token backups from n8n installation directories.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Child Process Chain from n8n Service
suggestion.rationale: Article implies full RCE but pipeline did not suggest post-exploitation behavioral detection. Once n8n node is compromised, attackers spawn reverse shells, system reconnaissance commands, or lateral movement utilities.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on node.exe or npm.exe spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, or sh with arguments matching reconnaissance patterns (whoami, systeminfo, ipconfig, id, uname) or reverse shell payloads (bash -i, powershell -nop -c, nc/ncat).

suggestion.title: n8n Vulnerable Version Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article headline emphasizes 'critical vulnerabilities' but no version ranges or affected builds mentioned in pipeline. Inventory detection for vulnerable n8n ≤ [version] is mandatory for patching prioritization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query package.json, npm list, or running process arguments to identify n8n versions matching known vulnerable ranges (CVE-2026-44789, 44790, 44791). Flag for urgent patching if versions ≤ published fix threshold.

suggestion.title: WordPress Plugin Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'vulnerability exposes websites to authentication bypass attacks'—exploitation is the entry vector—yet zero initial-access detections generated. Article should describe vulnerable plugin endpoints or exploit patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to WordPress plugin-specific admin/REST endpoints with suspicious parameter values, missing authentication, or known exploit signatures. Correlate with vulnerable plugin version from asset inventory to reduce false positives.

suggestion.title: Authentication Bypass Success Behavioral Detection
suggestion.rationale: Core impact is 'authentication bypass'—yet no detection logic for successful auth without valid credentials or from anomalous contexts following exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for successful WordPress admin/editor authentication lacking corresponding failed login noise, originating from IPs associated with prior exploitation probes, or occurring within seconds of plugin endpoint scanning.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Plugin Version Inventory Detection
suggestion.rationale: Without extracted plugin name and affected versions, organizations cannot inventory vulnerable installations. Pipeline should flag plugin instances below published patch version.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query software inventory for the vulnerable WordPress plugin by name and flag instances below the published patched version. Prioritize by exposure (public-facing WordPress + admin interface accessibility).

suggestion.title: Post-Bypass Unauthorized Administrative Action
suggestion.rationale: After auth bypass succeeds, attacker typically performs high-impact WordPress admin functions (plugin installation, user creation, code injection). Pipeline has no post-compromise behavioral detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WordPress admin logs (user creation, plugin upload, theme modification, option/setting changes) for unusual activity within minutes of exploitation-pattern HTTP requests or from IPs matching exploitation probes.

suggestion.title: Linux CONFIG_RXGK Kernel Configuration Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Successful exploitation requires running a Linux kernel with the CONFIG_RXGK configuration option.' No inventory detection for affected configuration was produced.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate Linux systems exposing /boot/config or parsing dmesg/kernel cmdline for CONFIG_RXGK=y. Flag systems running Fedora, Arch Linux, or openSUSE Tumbleweed with this option enabled and kernel version < patched release (patch date April 25, 2026 per CVE-2026-31635).

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Kernel Version Detection (CVE-2026-31635 / DirtyDecrypt)
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions patching occurred April 25, 2026, but no use case tracks vulnerable kernel versions. Article states vulnerability is in 'Linux kernel's rxgk module' and limits attack surface to distros 'that closely follow the latest upstream kernel releases.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference kernel versions reported by systems (uname, /proc/version) against advisory date (May 9, 2026 report date). Flag Fedora, Arch, openSUSE Tumbleweed systems running kernels released or patched before April 25, 2026, with CONFIG_RXGK enabled.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Attempt: rxgk_decrypt_skb COW Guard Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'rxgk pagecache write due to missing COW guard in rxgk_decrypt_skb' as the core vulnerability. PoC available (poc.c). No behavioral detection for exploitation attempts was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for userspace processes invoking eBPF or memory-mapping operations against /sys/kernel/debug/rxrpc or executing compiled PoC binaries. Correlate with subsequent privilege escalation (UID 0 process spawned from non-root parent in same session). Baseline tool execution (gcc, clang, make) on production servers as medium-confidence signal.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation Success: Root Shell from Unprivileged User
suggestion.rationale: Article states exploit 'allows attackers to gain root access.' No post-exploitation detection for successful privilege escalation was provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect spawning of /bin/bash, /bin/sh, or /bin/zsh with UID/EUID = 0 (root) from parent process with UID > 0 in same session. Exclude known privilege escalation tools (sudo, su with legitimate audit trail). High fidelity on systems where no privilege escalation is operationally expected.

suggestion.title: Kernel Module Load/Unload: esp4, esp6, rxrpc (Mitigation Evasion)
suggestion.rationale: Article provides mitigation: 'rmmod esp4 esp6 rxrpc' to disable modules triggering vulnerability. Detection should alert on module unload attempts, which may indicate either legitimate mitigation or attacker-driven evasion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution of 'rmmod esp4', 'rmmod esp6', 'rmmod rxrpc' or writes to /etc/modprobe.d/dirtyfrag.conf outside change-management windows. Correlate with absence of approved kernel patching ticket to distinguish mitigation from evasion.

suggestion.title: Related CVE Exploitation Chain: Dirty Frag, Fragnesia, Copy Fail Cross-Pollination
suggestion.rationale: Article notes DirtyDecrypt 'belongs to the same vulnerability class as several other root-escalation flaws... including Dirty Frag, Fragnesia, and Copy Fail' and warns 'attackers are now actively exploiting the Copy Fail vulnerability in the wild.' No cross-CVE correlation detection was generated despite explicit mention of active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate exploitation signals across related CVEs (Copy Fail, Dirty Frag, Fragnesia, DirtyDecrypt). If behavioral indicators for one LPE fire on the same host within 24 hours, escalate priority. Use CISA KEV list (Copy Fail added May 1, 2026) as baseline for active exploitation threat level.

suggestion.title: Twig template injection payload in Formie form submission to /actions/formie/submissions/submit
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Unauthenticated users could submit crafted values into Hidden fields (with Default value → Custom) that were evaluated as Twig during submission handling.' This is the exploit surface and should be the first detection target, correlating Twig delimiters with the specific vulnerable endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to /actions/formie/submissions/submit for Twig delimiters ({{ }}, {# #}, {% %}) in form field values. Alert on attempts to access Twig globals (_self, _context), Symfony classes, or execution functions (passthru, shell_exec). Baseline: zero Twig syntax in normal form submissions; flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Craft CMS .env, database config, or schema files accessed by PHP process post-SSTI
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could lead to serious compromise of the Craft site' but doesn't specify data-access patterns. SSTI enables local file inclusion; attackers extract .env, db.php, composer.json to harvest credentials. Not covered by existing UCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when PHP processes (spawned by web server) execute file-read operations (file_get_contents, include, require, fopen) targeting Craft configuration paths: .env, config/db.php, config/general.php, composer.json, schema files. Critical if within 2 minutes of SSTI payload submission or shell-spawning event.

suggestion.title: Database query anomaly: schema dump or admin/user record extraction after Formie SSTI
suggestion.rationale: RCE via SSTI implies database access. Article doesn't prescribe database-layer detection but 'serious compromise' implies data exfiltration. Expected chain: inject → execute → query → exfil. No existing UC covers this phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal Formie queries (form submissions, field definitions). Alert on anomalies: INFORMATION_SCHEMA dumps, SELECT * from admin_users, password/credential columns, or bulk exports executed by database connections originating from the web-server process within post-exploit window.

suggestion.title: Formie Hidden field configuration risk inventory: identify forms with Custom default values (pre-compromise scanning)
suggestion.rationale: Attack requires specific configuration: 'Hidden fields (with Default value → Custom)'. Proactive threat hunting should flag instances with this risky config before exploitation. Pre-incident detection not covered by reactive UCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Formie plugin config (database or YAML) to enumerate forms with Hidden field type + Custom default-value setting. Cross-reference with Craft instances exposed on internet (CVE scanning, Censys, Shodan). Prioritize for patching to <2.2.20. This is vulnerability-discovery detection, not attack-pattern detection.

suggestion.title: Outbound exfiltration from Craft CMS server: database dumps, environment vars, or credential blobs
suggestion.rationale: SSTI→RCE likely leads to data theft. Article: 'serious compromise' but doesn't prescribe exfiltration indicators. Expected final phase: attacker extracts database, config, user records to external host.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for large outbound transfers from Craft web server to non-whitelisted destinations. Flag database dump signatures (mysqldump output, gzip'd SQL), compressed archives, encoded payloads (base64), or credential-file contents in network streams. Alert if egress timing correlates with SSTI payload + RCE indicators.

suggestion.title: Privilege escalation: web-server process invoking sudo or escalating to root/db-user shell
suggestion.rationale: Article doesn't mention privilege escalation, but SSTI→RCE on a web-server process may be followed by escalation to database or root if sudoers misconfiguration exists. Completes the post-exploitation chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sudo commands, su invocations, or process escalation initiated by web-server user (www-data, apache, nginx, _www). Flag sudo -l enumerations, password-spray attempts, or escalation to root, database user, or Craft admin account. High fidelity if correlated with SSTI submission timing.

suggestion.title: Pip package manager installation of mistralai v2.4.6 from PyPI
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'mistralai PyPI package version 2.4.6 contains a malicious dropper' but lacks a detection for the initial-access moment when organizations first pull the malicious artifact via pip install. This is the supply-chain compromise entry point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for pip or python -m pip process execution with command-line arguments containing 'install mistralai' or version pinning to '2.4.6' during the vulnerability window (2026-05-18 onwards). Correlate with timestamp when package was uploaded to PyPI and subsequently quarantined.

suggestion.title: Python subprocess spawning shell interpreters immediately after mistralai import
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states dropper 'executes on import on Linux' but provides no UC for detecting Python child processes spawning unexpected shell commands, which would indicate the dropper activating post-import.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python interpreter (python, python3) spawning immediate child processes of bash, sh, or zsh within 1–2 seconds of mistralai module import. Focus on processes originating from site-packages or dist-packages directories and exclude known service accounts.

suggestion.title: Network beaconing to C2 IP 83.142.209.194 with Python dropper signatures
suggestion.rationale: C2 IP is known but no UC correlates outbound traffic with HTTP headers typical of Python dropper payloads (requests, urllib, aiohttp User-Agents) to distinguish C2 beaconing from legitimate traffic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound connections to 83.142.209.194 where initiating process is Python and HTTP User-Agent headers contain strings like 'python-requests', 'urllib3', or 'aiohttp'. Exclude legitimate mistralai API calls to official mistralai infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Suspicious .pyz or Python archive creation in /tmp or shared staging directories
suggestion.rationale: Article describes second-stage dropper as '/tmp/transformers.pyz' but provides no general-purpose UC for detecting Python archive files (.pyz, .zip) creation in world-writable directories outside normal CI/CD windows—useful for detecting similar supply-chain attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag file-creation events where FileName matches '*.pyz' or '*.zip' and FolderPath is '/tmp', '/var/tmp', or other shared directories, created by non-root, non-service accounts outside standard maintenance windows. Correlate with Python process activity.

suggestion.title: GitHub Personal Access Token Abuse – Unusual Commit, Clone, or Push Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'stolen GitHub token' enabled source code download. Need detection for anomalous GitHub API calls (bulk clones, rapid repo access) from previously unseen IPs or geographies using compromised token.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub audit logs for high-volume git clone/pull operations originating from single token within short timeframe. Correlate with token creation date and user baseline access patterns. Alert on repos accessed outside normal developer scope (e.g., all private repos in single session).

suggestion.title: Large-Scale Private Repository Exfiltration Pattern
suggestion.rationale: 'Downloaded its source code' indicates bulk exfiltration. Detect when single user/token downloads complete repository archives or clones multiple repos sequentially.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag git export/archive operations or sequential clone operations targeting 3+ private repos in <5 minutes. Correlate total bytes downloaded, destination IP reputation, and whether destination is known GitHub CI/CD provider. Cross-reference with VCS rate-limit violations.

suggestion.title: CoinbaseCartel Threat Actor Infrastructure Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'CoinbaseCartel' as claimant on extortion portal ('DLS'). Map known IOCs: DLS domain, threat actor aliases (ShinyHunters, Lapsus$), ransomware variants (shinysp1d3r), command & control infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate known CoinbaseCartel DLS URLs, registered domains, and infrastructure against proxy/DNS logs and email gateways. Alert on employee access to extortion portal or communications with known threat actor accounts/email addresses.

suggestion.title: shinysp1d3r ESXi Ransomware Execution and Snapshot Deletion
suggestion.rationale: Article states gang 'deploys an in-memory tool called shinysp1d3r to encrypt VMware ESXi targets and disable snapshots.' Need detection for file encryption patterns and snapshot removal on ESXi hypervisors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ESXi logs for bulk VM snapshot deletions or disables, combined with unusual process execution (especially memory-resident tools). Alert on rapid file encryption/modification on ESXi datastores, especially .vmdk files. Baseline snapshot deletion frequency per host.

suggestion.title: Social Engineering and Credential Phishing Precursors – Compromised Credentials Workflow
suggestion.rationale: Article notes gang 'gain access to target networks via social engineering, various forms of phishing, and compromised credentials.' Detect phishing campaigns and credential compromise signals before token theft occurs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate phishing email detections (credential-harvesting URLs, lookalike domains) with failed MFA attempts, password spray patterns, and unusual VPN/SSO access. Flag employees receiving phishing + subsequent failed auth as high-risk. Track credential breaches via OSINT feeds.

suggestion.title: Post-Incident Bulk Credential Revocation and Token Invalidation Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'invalidated the compromised credentials and implemented additional security measures.' Detect mass credential resets, token revocations, and PAT regenerations as indicator of breach response.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk token revocation events, simultaneous PAT regenerations across GitHub organization, or coordinated password resets across multiple systems in short timeframe. Baseline organization's normal rate of credential changes; alert on 5x deviation in <1 hour.

suggestion.title: NGINX Exploit Payload Detection — HTTP Request Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Hackers Actively Exploiting Critical NGINX RCE Vulnerability' yet pipeline extracted zero use cases. At minimum, should detect malformed HTTP requests, unusual query parameters, or request path traversal patterns typical of NGINX RCE payloads (e.g., CVE-2023-44487 HTTP/2 CONTINUATION frame abuse, or CVE-2022-41741 off-by-one buffer overflow).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor NGINX access and error logs for anomalous HTTP requests with oversized headers, repeated CONTINUATION frames, path traversal attempts (../), or unrecognized HTTP/2 sequences. Baseline request sizes and frame patterns; alert on statistical outliers and known RCE payload signatures.

suggestion.title: NGINX Process Spawning Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Successful RCE would result in arbitrary command execution. Pipeline should surface detection of unexpected child processes spawned from nginx worker/master processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when nginx (uid=www-data, nginx user) spawns unusual children: /bin/bash, /bin/sh, curl, wget, python, perl, or reverse-shell indicators. Baseline normal nginx child processes; anomalies suggest post-exploitation command execution.

suggestion.title: NGINX Configuration Modification Detection
suggestion.rationale: Persistent NGINX exploits often modify nginx.conf or drop webshells into web root. Pipeline omitted detections for config tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor /etc/nginx/nginx.conf, /etc/nginx/conf.d/, and web root directories for unauthorized modifications. Alert on timestamp changes, permission changes, or unexpected includes/proxy directives. Combine with process monitoring for nginx reload/restart commands.

suggestion.title: Reverse Proxy Misuse — Outbound C2 Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article describes active exploitation 'in the wild.' Compromised NGINX instances often become C2 nodes or proxies for lateral movement. Pipeline should detect anomalous outbound connections from nginx processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline typical NGINX outbound connections (upstream servers, DNS). Alert on unexpected outbound TCP/UDP to non-whitelisted IPs, especially on unusual ports (4444, 5555, 8888) or to known C2 infrastructure. Monitor for encrypted tunnel indicators (OpenVPN, SSH reverse tunnel).

suggestion.title: Storm-2949: Lateral movement via stolen cloud credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article states threat moved 'from identity compromise to large-scale data theft' and 'exploit[ed] trusted systems to operate undetected'—indicates authenticated access to multiple cloud resources using stolen identities.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for interactive logins from unusual geographies or IPs, concurrent sessions from same account across regions, or authentication from residential proxies. Establish baseline of normal SaaS login patterns per user and alert on statistical outliers.

suggestion.title: Cloud service discovery by compromised identity
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'cloud-wide breach'—implies attacker enumerated available cloud services and storage after credential theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sequences of failed API calls or permission-denied responses from single identity across multiple services in short window (cloud service probing). Flag List commands on SharePoint/OneDrive executed by accounts with minimal historical activity.

suggestion.title: Bulk email and cloud storage exfiltration without malware
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes attack succeeded 'without using malware'—must rely on native cloud APIs; describes 'large-scale data theft' via 'trusted systems'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect high-volume downloads from SharePoint/OneDrive libraries or cloud storage exports to external accounts. Alert on mass email forwarding rules or unusual Export-Mailbox cmdlets from interactive sessions. Monitor for API bulk-read operations at scale.

suggestion.title: Persistent access via cloud automation and OAuth abuse
suggestion.rationale: Operating undetected in 'trusted systems' suggests leveraging cloud-native persistence mechanisms; articles on this pattern typically involve OAuth tokens or service principals for long-term access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for new OAuth app consent grants to suspicious scopes (Mail.Read, Files.Read). Alert on service principal creation by human users or unusual credential additions to app registrations. Flag new forwarding rules or delegation grant from compromised account.

suggestion.title: Credential compromise detection—internal phishing or password spray
suggestion.rationale: Article begins with 'compromised identity'—how credentials were stolen is critical to initial detection; description lacks malware suggests social engineering or brute-force.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline failed login attempts per user. Alert on spike in failed logins followed by successful auth from new device/geography. Monitor for suspicious browser or client used in initial compromise. Flag accounts with successful login after ≥10 failures in 24h.

suggestion.title: Monitor for re-activation of sinkholed Operation Ramz C2 infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article documents 'cybercrime networks' and 201 arrests, implying captured command-and-control servers and malware delivery domains. These should be tracked for re-registration, DNS pointer updates, or successor-actor reuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on DNS resolution or network connections to previously-documented C2 domains from Operation Ramz. Monitor for dynamic DNS updates, WHOIS registration changes, or hosting provider migrations of arrested group infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Detect execution of known malware families from arrested network
suggestion.rationale: INTERPOL operation captures malware samples and hash signatures used by the criminal network. Article should document specific malware families or PE hashes to alert on in enterprise environments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process execution or file write of known malware hashes/families from Operation Ramz. Cross-correlate with phishing email metadata patterns and delivery mechanisms documented in arrest records.

suggestion.title: Track credential theft patterns and stolen account re-use
suggestion.rationale: Large cybercrime network operations captured by law enforcement yield lists of compromised credentials, payment accounts, and customer PII. Article likely contains credential pairs, email accounts, or stolen financial data—must drive SOC credential monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on login attempts using credentials from captured Operation Ramz databases. Monitor for anomalous authentication patterns (impossible travel, impossible login time) from seized email accounts. Cross-reference leaked credential material against internal account repositories.

suggestion.title: Correlate phishing campaign infrastructure with arrested actor TTP
suggestion.rationale: Cybercrime networks use consistent phishing infrastructure (sender domains, typosquatting patterns, email hosting, spoofed brands). Article should document attacker's common phishing techniques and sender patterns to detect similar future campaigns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on emails matching documented phishing patterns, sender domain techniques, or URL-shortening services used by Operation Ramz actors. Monitor for lookalike domains and recipient targeting patterns from arrest records.

suggestion.title: Monitor for dark web marketplace re-emergence of arrested group services
suggestion.rationale: Cybercrime networks often advertise stolen data, malware samples, and botnet access on dark web forums. Article should document which marketplaces or forums were used, enabling monitoring for successor operations or data dump announcements.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor dark web marketplaces and paste sites for data dumps, credential sales, or botnets associated with Operation Ramz actors. Alert on vendor account re-emergence or successor claims to inherited infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Detect lateral movement in compromised enterprise networks
suggestion.rationale: Cybercrime networks that achieve enterprise compromise typically perform lateral movement, privilege escalation, and data exfiltration. Article should document common lateral movement techniques (RDP abuse, Kerberos attacks, share enumeration) used by the group.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on inter-host RDP connections from compromised systems, Kerberoasting attempts, or Windows share enumeration matching Operation Ramz lateral movement patterns. Monitor for non-standard service account activation or credential delegation anomalies.

suggestion.title: SparkCat Crypto Stealer Installation from App Store
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'we discovered several apps on Google Play and the App Store that contained a new version of the SparkCat crypto stealer.' Direct evidence of supply-chain infection via official distribution channels.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for app package installations from Google Play or App Store that execute crypto wallet interactions or clipboard access patterns. Flag APK manifests requesting PERMISSION_GET_ACCOUNTS or PERMISSION_READ_CLIPBOARD combined with network activity to known stealer C2. Monitor for Rust library loading within Android app process memory.

suggestion.title: Custom Dalvik-Like VM for Payload Decryption
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'obfuscated Rust library was decrypted using a Dalvik-like virtual machine custom-built by the attackers.' Detection of custom VM execution is critical for defense evasion baseline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect loading of non-standard runtime environments or virtual machine interpreters within mobile app processes. Flag child process spawning from app_process that executes native libraries (.so files) with entropy indicative of encryption. Monitor for file I/O patterns consistent with runtime decryption (read encrypted blob, write unencrypted to memory/temp).

suggestion.title: Kimwolf Botnet Proxy Network Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article reports: 'Synthient researchers identified a link between the notorious Kimwolf botnet and the IPIDEA proxy network.' Directly establishes C2 infrastructure requiring detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for network connections from mobile devices to known IPIDEA proxy network IP ranges or domain registrants. Flag HTTP/HTTPS traffic with Kimwolf-specific headers or user-agent strings. Detect beaconing patterns to proxy infrastructure with irregular but consistent intervals indicative of botnet polling.

suggestion.title: Mobile Banking Trojan Package Proliferation Detection
